ai.description: *Gegeneophis primus* is a slender, 20–25 cm long caecilian with a uniform dark brown body. It is distinguished by a lack of secondary annuli and a terminal shield on the tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gegeneophis primus* is uniquely distinguished from other Indian caecilians by its distinctively high primary annular count (125–132) and the absence of secondary grooves.
ai.habitat: *Gegeneophis primus* inhabits moist, shaded soil within evergreen forests and cardamom plantations in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 800 and 1,100 meters.
ai.behavior: The Malabar Cardamom Geg is primarily nocturnal, spending its active hours burrowing through moist soil in search of earthworms and other subterranean invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gegeneophis primus* is oviparous and exhibits maternal care. Females lay a small clutch of eggs in underground nests during the pre-monsoon season (April–May).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gegeneophis primus* is endemic to the Western Ghats in Kerala, India, where it is found at elevations between 800 and 1,100 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Gegeneophis primus* consists of a series of low-pitched, pulsed notes emitted from within moist soil or leaf litter in cardamom plantations.
